title: An Octopus Has Three Hearts
description:
An octopus has three hearts: two push blood through the gills and one sends it to the rest of the body. When the octopus swims, the body heart is reported to pause, which may be one reason octopuses prefer to crawl. Their blood is blue because it uses copper-based hemocyanin instead of iron-based hemoglobin.

Sources: Live Science, 'How many hearts does an octopus have?'; general octopus physiology references. The 'pause while swimming' explanation is a hypothesis; details vary by source.

Have you ever seen an octopus swim? Tell us in the comments.
